static.solution: \int\,u\,v'\,dx = u\cdot v - \int u'\,v\,dx) with u = t^2 and v' = \sin(t), so that u' = 2t and v = - \cos(t). Then \int\,2 t^2\,\sin(t)\,dt = -2 t^2 \cos(t) + \int 4 t \cos(t)\,dt, and we can find the second integral by using integration by parts again. Here, we let u = t and v' = \cos(t), so that u' = 1 and v = \sin(t), and \int\,2 t^2\,\sin(t)\,dt = -2 t^2 \cos(t) + 4 t \sin(t) - \int\,4 \sin(t)\,dt = -2 t^2 \cos(t) + 4 t \sin(t) + 4 \cos(t) + C.
